subject.title: PR1/5 durable core: RFC and release-head docs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt and publicly document this proposed shared durable-core substrate as the architectural base for the four downstream implementation PRs?
rationale: The patch is documentation-only and internally cautious, but the decision determines a broad new core persistence boundary across tasks, sessions, subagents, wake obligations, recovery, and delivery; repository policy and tests cannot choose that product architecture.

options.title: Review as design first
options.body: Keep the implementation stack paused and move or link the RFC to a canonical design discussion until maintainers approve its exact boundary against TaskFlow and existing durable owners.

options.title: Sponsor the durable core
options.body: Approve the RFC as the intended core direction, retain the public pages, and review downstream PRs against explicit non-duplication, migration, and ownership gates.

options.title: Keep existing owners
options.body: Decline the new substrate and address remaining durability gaps within TaskFlow, task, session, delivery, and plugin-owned contracts.

recommendation.title: Review as design first
recommendation.body: Keep the implementation stack paused and move or link the RFC to a canonical design discussion until maintainers approve its exact boundary against TaskFlow and existing durable owners.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects steipete to the repository's core-versus-plugin scope decisions and TaskFlow documentation.
